sharing-excess.v: Working with Sharing Excess, a nonprofit dedicated to addressing food insecurity, has allowed me to use design to amplify their mission and impact. Supporting nonprofits like Sharing Excess is central to my work, and I take pride in creating marketing collateral and graphics that drive awareness and engagement for meaningful causes.

My projects with Sharing Excess have spanned print and digital platforms, including flyers for community events, vendor appreciation initiatives, and holiday celebrations. For their vendor appreciation events and holiday parties in Philadelphia and New York, I developed cohesive visual materials that reflected the nonprofit’s mission while fostering a sense of unity. From reusable bag designs to impactful social media graphics, each asset was carefully crafted to resonate with audiences and highlight the vital role Sharing Excess plays in reducing food waste and supporting communities.

The design strategy for these projects prioritized clarity and accessibility, creating visuals that engage audiences and inspire action. Bold, minimalist billboards carried succinct messages to capture attention, while social media carousels broke down complex data into digestible and compelling narratives. A consistent visual identity across all materials helped establish trust and recognition, reinforcing Sharing Excess’s nonprofit mission and amplifying their efforts.

One highlight of my work with Sharing Excess was designing materials for their partnership with Mt. Joy, a nationwide food drive during the band’s headlining tour. These designs balanced Sharing Excess’s branding with the band’s aesthetic, successfully rallying volunteers, encouraging donations, and demonstrating the power of collaboration between nonprofits and creative partnerships.

Supporting nonprofits like Sharing Excess allows me to align my creative expertise with causes that make a tangible difference. From large-scale campaigns to everyday marketing needs, my designs aim to foster engagement, inspire action, and contribute to meaningful change. Working with Sharing Excess has been a deeply rewarding opportunity to use design as a force for good.

bna-social-media-design.v: Working with the Black Nashville Assembly (BNA), I support their initiatives by producing marketing collateral and graphics for both print and digital needs. My work includes designing flyers for student opportunities, town hall meetings, and community support events, helping amplify their mission and engage the community effectively.

The flyers I design serve as a key tool in promoting BNA’s various initiatives. These include student programs, public events, and community support efforts. Each flyer is carefully crafted to be visually appealing and informative, ensuring they effectively communicate the intended message and drive participation.

For BNA’s projects, I create logos and supporting visual elements designed to be responsive and adaptable across different formats. These logos appear on materials such as T-shirts, social media graphics, and printed collateral, helping build a cohesive and recognizable brand identity. The flexibility of these designs ensures they maintain their impact across a variety of applications while reinforcing the organization’s mission.

In 2024, the Black Nashville Assembly and the Southern Movement Committee launched the Varsity Spending Plan (VSP) to secure funding for community programming and restorative justice. As part of this initiative, I designed a comprehensive range of marketing materials, including responsive logos and event-specific graphics. These designs were featured on T-shirts, social media platforms, and posters, effectively raising awareness about the campaign.

The promotional materials were instrumental in increasing engagement, boosting attendance at key events, and fostering pride and unity among supporters. The VSP successfully secured $1 million in funding, with $250,000 directed toward community programming and restorative justice, and $750,000 allocated to the creation of the Office of Youth Safety. This achievement highlights how strategic design can amplify advocacy efforts and create tangible impact.

orretts-sports-legacy.v: Working with Orretts, I designed a logo that would be used as the symbol for sports trading cards. They wanted something more aligned with the simplicity of the Nike logo—memorable and easy to draw. They also wanted it to resemble a DNA helix.  I was reached out to by Christopher Strachan, who founded the non-profit Kickin’ It for a Cause. Kickin' It for a Cause provides basic necessities to systematically disadvantaged people all over the globe while offering the education needed for these individuals to excel in life. The organization supplies essentials like food, water, and footwear, while also educating people on complex topics such as mental and physical health, and environmental awareness.  Christopher Strachan and Nick Drbal, the co-founders, reached out to me to create a symbol for their new venture, Orrett’s Sports Legacy—a brand focused on sports memorabilia.

Named after Christopher Strachan’s father, the company is a tribute to the values he instilled in Chris: hard work, pride in heritage, and a relentless pursuit of excellence. Orrett hailed from Jamaica, and the vibrant energy of the island, its colors, and its flag are at the heart of the brand. Christopher has a deep love for sports and memorabilia, a passion that has only deepened as his relationships have grown. His connection with Stephen Curry, one of the greatest athletes of our time, gave him a unique perspective on bridging the gap between sports legends and their fans. With an understanding of the brand, its goals, and its primary focus, I had my starting point. I began by creating three written concepts to better grasp what they envisioned. Using frequently mentioned keywords and terms, I developed three directions, varying in style and complexity, but all simple in their own right. After reviewing the provided concepts, Chris and Nick noted that they didn’t want the logo to be “basketball” or “ball” themed. Based on the feedback, we leaned more toward the modern pictorial DNA mark, which features a simple yet instantly recognizable representation of a DNA strand.

You can see those designs below. For numbers one through four, I kept things simple, focusing solely on geometric shapes to create a modern feel. For numbers five, six, thirteen, and fourteen, I took a more characteristic approach while ensuring the designs remained recognizable. Additionally, I brought in another designer to work on numbers seven and eight, bringing in a different perspective and giving Chris and Nick more options to consider. Chris mentioned that his favorites were 5, 7, 9, and 16, with 5 being his most favorite. He said, "I like the simplicity in 5 and 9, I like how it's easily traceable. I think you can clearly see the DNA aspect of it. 7 feels fun to look at, so it jumped out at me. I like how 9 was simple but different." However, after sitting with it for a few days, he wasn’t in love with it. “I’m really looking for something easily traceable and recognizable, like the Nike swoosh,” Chris noted.

With the feedback in mind and a deeper understanding of what Chris and Nick were envisioning, I sent through three new designs. They ended up choosing the direction below. Although they liked this option, they felt the logo still needed a bit more character. We hopped on a quick call to discuss ways we could make the logo more visually interesting.

Some ideas we discussed included using double lines within the shape, experimenting with line thickness, exploring the negative space within the logo, and trying different variations for the ends/edges of the logo.

After reviewing the revised concepts, Chris and Nick decided to go with the initial direction. The final logo is a play on the Jamaican flag, taking the paths from the top and bottom triangles of the flag, rounding out the peaks of both triangles, and intersecting them to create the helix. Just as the Nike logo abstracts the wings of the Greek goddess of victory, this mark follows a similar approach. By merging inspiration from the Jamaican flag with DNA symbolism, this logo embodies the idea that "legacy is in one's DNA," staying deeply representative of the brand's core values. Running the logo through the WIPO brand database, I found nothing resembling the logo—not even close. The logo feels familiar, but there’s nothing quite like it.

"Swoop, Thank you brother. We are so happy to work on more.
Thanks for being diligently."
- Nick Drbal
"Swoop, you bodied this! Preciate you my man! We are gonna take this thing global!" - Christopher Seezy

adobe.v: Working with Adobe, I was brought in to create social media content and creative materials, driving engagement across their respective social media channels and fostering engagement for their flagship applications and events through tutorial videos, packaging design, and "day in the life" style content tailored for Photoshop, Adobe Max, and Adobe Illustrator. For the deliverables created for the Adobe MAX 2023, I collaborated with 3D designer Masong3D, providing art direction to bring the concepts to life. The primary goal of the project was to design content that would raise awareness and drive traffic.

the-doors-merchandise-design.v: For this project, I was tasked with designing merchandise and concepts for The Doors' management. Drawing inspiration from vintage band merchandise, I sought to create timeless designs that would resonate with fans over the years. The focus was on screen-printed designs exclusively for black T-shirts and merchandise, which are highly sought after.

sandy-alex-g-show-poster.v: While working with Third Man Records, I got the opportunity to create a show poster for Sandy Alex G. Packaged within his branding, he often incorporates doodled characters to support his concepts and ideas. My goal here was to expand upon that and introduce additional elements to push the narrative.

tortuga-music-festival-poster.v: Held to raise awareness and support ocean conservation, this music festival takes place on the beaches of Florida. For their Festival poster, I sought to create a piece that captures the character of the event.

wilder-woods-tour-poster.v: Wilder Woods is a member of American Christian Rock Band NEEDTOBREATHE. Working with Future Shirts, I created this poster for his debut tour. The poster is inspired by the Bauhaus and Art Deco movements.

lightwave-solar.v: Working with LightWave Solar I was brought in to help create designs and graphics that could be used to increase brand awareness and gain referrals from customers, friends, and visitors who come across businesses or cars. We wanted to stay away from anything too childlike; we wanted this to appeal to adults. The goal was to keep things clean and minimal while still making it fun.

We wanted the designs to work well across various mediums. This idea inspired us (the client and me) to create two versions of the logo that could be used interchangeably across apparel, accessories, and store signage. We created versions with transparent backgrounds that work for vinyl cuts, screen printing, and can easily be uploaded to print provider platforms for things like stickers, water bottles, and custom requests. I also created mockups that could be sent to print providers as references.

Here are the initial concepts proposed to the client based on the feedback provided from the written briefs. I outsourced the illustration for the solar panel and worked it into a badge shape. We wanted to create something modular, and a badge shape fit the bill perfectly. These directions varied in complexity, ranging from minimal Swiss-style design to something more illustrative and vintage. Out of the bunch, we moved forward with 7, 11, and 15, making minor changes and adjustments along the way. I put the designs through a few rounds of tightening, ensuring the micro and macro spacing, is balanced within the designs.

At the beginning of this process, I like to allow my ideas to marinate, sketch, and write out all of the ideas that I have. These sketches then serve as my starting point for creating written concepts to propose to the client, these written concepts consist of ideas from my sketchbook I use words and supporting inspiration to describe the ideas instead of the sketches themselves. This helps us hone in on what we liked and didn’t like about each direction, which clarifies the overall vision.

hot-country-knights-tour-poster.v: Working with Hot Country Knights, I was tasked with creating a poster for an up-and-coming tour. Through a letterpress style reminiscent of early and vintage show posters renowned in Nashville and country music, I aimed to capture an essence and aesthetic that pays homage to the city's famous and local print shops.

little-river-band-merchandise-design.v: Working closely with the Little River Band, I crafted merchandise to promote their upcoming album and tour. The design aimed to strike a chord with their dedicated fanbase, capturing the essence of their music and resonating with their audience.

lance-bass-space-camp.v: Making a guest appearance on Single Parents, Lance Bass wanted a shirt design that reflects his role. In the popular ABC show, The former NSYNC member plays a space camp instructor with a passion for space and the performing arts.
